summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks (AFP reported none on Iranian targets since early September). Trump said on Oct 8 the US would not resume strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.value: About US$117 (expiring December contract); about US$113.6 for January
status.note: The December contract, which expires on Oct 30, was near US$117.15 in early US trading (Kitco, about 9:10 a.m. ET), on course for a monthly gain of about 13%; Trading Economics showed Brent at US$113.61, up 2.5% on the day, and Yahoo Finance put Brent near US$113 and WTI near US$104 after the US open.

updates.text: UKMTO reported that a vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile about 40 nautical miles south of Lavan Island at 1800 GMT; it did not mention a mine or say the vessel was a tanker.

The IRGC Navy said a fourth oil tanker, a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels, hit a mine and caught fire on an 'unauthorised southern route' through the strait; the claim has not been independently confirmed.
Trump said the war with Iran is "going to get wrapped up soon" and that the US needs a "guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon."

The Revolutionary Guard said a supertanker carrying two million barrels stopped after striking a naval mine, calling it the third tanker to explode and catch fire that day; the claim has not been independently confirmed.

Oman's Maritime Security Centre said it evacuated 25 crew from the burning Panama-flagged crude tanker RITI in the Strait of Hormuz; it was not confirmed whether it was one of the tankers Iran's Revolutionary Guard said were stopped or hit mines.
sources: Al Jazeera: Oman rescues 25 from burning oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz

updates.text: UKMTO reported that a small boat attached two explosive devices above the waterline of a tanker leaving the strait about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman; the blasts caused an engine-room fire, the crew was safe and the ship continued to its next port. Reuters, citing maritime security sources, named the tanker as Louise 1.
sources: Greek City Times (citing UKMTO, Reuters, AFP), Oct 30

updates.text: US Central Command's Adm. Brad Cooper disputed Iran's account of the tanker incidents, saying the main shipping lanes were cleared of mines and rejecting the Revolutionary Guard's claim to have seized a US drone.

Iran's navy said two oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the eastern part of the strait and that it destroyed an unmanned drone craft east of the strait; the claims have not been independently confirmed.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
